finalText:
**Found it — `computeTotal` rounds twice.**

`engine.js:24` rounds the percent discount to cents **in USD**, before converting. The real contract, which the test spells out, is to round once at the very end in the order's own currency.

So `2 × $9.99` minus 10% is `17.982`, but the engine flattens it to `17.98` first. That lost half-cent gets multiplied by the exchange rate and tips the final rounding.

That's why it looks random. It only shows up when the rate pushes the lost fraction across a boundary:

| Currency | Slips? |
| --- | --- |
| USD, EUR | never |
| GBP, CAD | every percent cart |
| JPY | only some baskets |

Every one of the 10 failures has a percent coupon, and every one is a cent **low**. Stacking isn't the trigger — the percent coupon is. Flat-only carts are all fine, since `$5` off adds no fraction.

Fix is to drop the `round(..., 2)` on lines 24 and 27 and let line 31 do the only rounding. I checked that against all 40 cases and it matches. Want me to apply it?
